## F09.definition-format — Definition format

Definition: File layout and frontmatter fields of a custom agent.
- claude-code [supported, verified] Subagents are defined in .claude/agents/; each markdown file in agents/ defines a subagent with its own system prompt, tool access, and optionally its own model. A subagent type can come from the project, user, managed, or plugin subagent scope, and a definition can be reused as a delegated subagent and as an agent team teammate. | ev: E-claude-code-02210, E-claude-code-06823, E-claude-code-01541
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Subagent role configuration lives under [agents] in config.toml, which holds multi-agent settings and custom role declarations (scalar setting names are reserved and can't be used as custom role names). A commented sample sets config_file = "./agents/reviewer.toml", relative to the config.toml that defines it. The sandbox configuration can be overridden for individual custom agents. | ev: E-codex-cli-00966, E-codex-cli-02974, E-codex-cli-00609, E-codex-cli-00025
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Custom agents are defined using Markdown files, called agent profiles, that specify what expertise the agent should have, what tools it can use, and any specific instructions. A custom agent is eligible for inference unless infer is set to false; work it performs is carried out by a subagent with its own context window. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00608, E-copilot-cli-00085, E-copilot-cli-00457
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] Custom agent files use the `.agent.md` extension, with an optional YAML header that configures the agent and a Markdown body that provides its instructions. The `tools` metadata field sets the available tools, and `hooks` in `.agent.md` frontmatter scope hooks to that agent. Example workspace agent: `.github/agents/researcher.agent.md`. | limit: `hooks` in `.agent.md` frontmatter 'Runs only for that custom agent in the Local harness.' | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00116, E-copilot-vscode-02052, E-copilot-vscode-01764, E-copilot-vscode-00152
- cursor [supported, verified] Custom subagents are markdown files added to .cursor/agents/; plugin agents are markdown files in agents/. The model field in a subagent's YAML frontmatter can be set to a specific model ID; custom subagents default to inherit, which uses the parent agent's model. In the cloud API each custom subagent entry requires name, description and prompt, plus an optional model. | ev: E-cursor-03976, E-cursor-01457, E-cursor-03575, E-cursor-00390
- gemini-cli [supported, verified] Remote subagents are defined as Markdown files (.md) with YAML frontmatter; the name field is required and must be a valid slug (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only). Extensions add agent definition files (.md) to an agents/ directory in the extension root. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01748, E-gemini-cli-01749, E-gemini-cli-01349
- grok-build [supported, verified] Types are added or overridden under `.grok/agents/` or `~/.grok/agents/` (managed with `/config-agents`, alias `/agents`). `GROK_AGENT` takes a built-in agent name, a profile, or an absolute path to an agent definition. Personas are behavioral overlays only, defined under `[subagents.personas]` or `.grok/personas/*.toml`. | ev: E-grok-build-00315, E-grok-build-00154, E-grok-build-00387
- grok-bot [supported, unverified] A Bot has a name, a label and a description, set under Bot settings. The description is the Bot's job: it tells the Bot what to work on, which sources to use, and when to ask you first. Only the Bot's owner can change these. | ev: E-grok-bot-00465, E-grok-bot-00540, E-grok-bot-00604

## F09.tool-allowlist — Tool allow-list

Definition: How an agent's tools are restricted.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] AgentDefinition's tools field is an array of allowed tool names; if omitted, the agent inherits every tool available to subagents. A teammate from a subagent definition is limited to the definition's tools list. On the CLI, --tools restricts which tools are available. By default a subagent does not get the Agent tool itself, to prevent recursion. | ev: E-claude-code-00600, E-claude-code-01542, E-claude-code-07021, E-claude-code-07387
- codex-cli [supported, verified] A custom agent file can include other supported config.toml keys, such as model, model_reasoning_effort, sandbox_mode, mcp_servers, and skills.config. Agents can be given different roles and tools, for example one with MCP servers that fetch production logs for debugging. Tool restrictions or permissions in imported skills and agents are listed as something to review after importing. | ev: E-codex-cli-00044, E-codex-cli-03170, E-codex-cli-04047
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] The tools field lists the tools available to a custom agent; default ["*"] (all tools), and including * anywhere grants every tool, e.g. ["view", "*"]. By default agents have all tools; restricting access adds a tools specification to the agent file. A reviewer agent would typically not be permitted to change code files. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01063, E-copilot-cli-02504, E-copilot-cli-02520
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] A custom agent's available tools are set with the `tools` metadata field, which prompt files also use. The field can include built-in tools, tool sets, MCP tools, or tools contributed by extensions, and `‹server name›/*` includes all tools of an MCP server. A tool set is a reusable collection of tools referenced as a single entity in custom agents. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00120, E-copilot-vscode-01764, E-copilot-vscode-01773
- cursor [partial, verified] The SDK tools option allowlists the built-in tools offered to the model, and disallowed_tools removes tools and keeps the rest. In a subagent definition, readonly: true (default false) runs the subagent with restricted write permissions (no file edits, no state-changing shell commands). Subagents can be configured with custom prompts, tool access, and models. | limit: SDK tools and disallowed_tools: both are local agents only for now, and neither persists on the agent; pass them again on resume. | ev: E-cursor-01184, E-cursor-01410, E-cursor-01468
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] The optional tools frontmatter array lists tool names the agent can use; wildcards are * (all tools), mcp_* (all MCP tools) and mcp_server_* (all tools from a server). If omitted, it inherits all tools from the parent session. The subagent only has access to the tools you explicitly (quote truncated). Even with the * wildcard it is unable to see or invoke other agents. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00419, E-gemini-cli-00498, E-gemini-cli-00499, E-gemini-cli-00428
- grok-build [supported, unverified] The built-in `explore` type is read, list, and search only (no shell, no edits). | ev: E-grok-build-00313

## F09.per-agent-model — Per-agent model

Definition: Setting a model on a single agent. (lever class: model)
- claude-code [supported, verified] AgentDefinition.model overrides the model for one agent and accepts an alias such as fable, opus, sonnet, haiku or inherit (inherit uses the main model), or a full model ID. Each markdown file in agents/ can optionally set its own model; for simple subagent tasks the docs suggest model: haiku. When omitted, Claude Code uses the subagent model order. | ev: E-claude-code-00825, E-claude-code-00602, E-claude-code-07490, E-claude-code-06823
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Model can be set per agent: a custom agent file may include a model key, agents.default_subagent_model sets the default for spawned agents, and an explicit spawn model takes precedence over that default. | ev: E-codex-cli-00044, E-codex-cli-00612, E-codex-cli-00041
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] A custom agent definition can specify the model used when that agent runs. A per-agent model configuration object, keyed by agent name, takes an optional model and a modelPolicy of preferred or required. If a subagent uses a custom agent profile that specifies a particular AI model, that model is used by the subagent. | limit: The built-in research agent is hard-coded to use a particular AI model, and its model selection is not configurable via the /model command (E-copilot-cli-00259). | ev: E-copilot-cli-01270, E-copilot-cli-01405, E-copilot-cli-00177, E-copilot-cli-00259
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] A custom agent's model property takes a single model name or a prioritized list, tried in order until an available one is found; if unset, the currently selected model is used. A custom agent run as a subagent can override the tools and model. Preferred models can be pinned in prompt files or custom agent definitions. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00125, E-copilot-vscode-01007, E-copilot-vscode-00280
- cursor [supported, verified] A subagent's model field takes inherit (the default) or a specific model ID. Custom subagents default to inherit, using the parent agent's model, unless the model field in the YAML frontmatter sets one. Cloud Agent API customSubagents entries also take an optional model. | ev: E-cursor-01409, E-cursor-01457, E-cursor-00390
- gemini-cli [supported, verified] The `model` entry takes a specific model to use (for example, `gemini-3-preview`) and defaults to `inherit` (uses the main session model). You can target specific subagents with custom model settings. An example under `settings.json` `agents.overrides` forces a specific model. The `/agents` entry says you can 'adjust its model, temperature, or execution limits'. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00421, E-gemini-cli-00506, E-gemini-cli-00396, E-gemini-cli-00462
- grok-build [supported, verified] [subagents.models] maps each subagent to a model id, giving per-subagent model routing. | ev: E-grok-build-00210

## F09.per-agent-effort — Per-agent effort

Definition: Setting reasoning effort on a single agent. (lever class: effort)
- claude-code [supported, verified] A subagent's effort field sets its reasoning effort and overrides the session effort level; it defaults to inheriting from the session. Options are low, medium, high, xhigh and max, and AgentDefinition also accepts a number. Available levels depend on the model. Set in subagent markdown frontmatter or on AgentDefinition. | ev: E-claude-code-14746, E-claude-code-00834, E-claude-code-00180, E-claude-code-11518
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Reasoning effort can be set per agent: a custom agent file can set model_reasoning_effort, and agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort sets the default reasoning effort for spawned agents. An explicit spawn effort takes precedence over that default. | ev: E-codex-cli-00033, E-codex-cli-00040, E-codex-cli-00613, E-codex-cli-00041
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] Custom agent frontmatter reasoningEffort sets that agent's default reasoning effort (for example low, medium, high); unset, it inherits the outer agent's effort. The per-agent settings.json entry accepts effortLevel, which can be set to inherit. Precedence, highest first: per-call value, then settings.json subagents override, then the agent definition. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01062, E-copilot-cli-01270, E-copilot-cli-01064, E-copilot-cli-01271

## F09.nesting-rules — Nesting rules

Definition: Whether and how deep agents can spawn agents. (lever class: parallelism)
- claude-code [partial, verified] Subagents can also spawn subagents of their own; the docs link a section on capping nesting depth, concurrency and spend. For messages from a nested subagent, a field gives the agentId of the subagent that spawned it (requires Claude Code v2.1.202 or later). Another page says a subagent gets most of the parent's tools, minus by default the Agent tool itself, to prevent recursion. | limit: Two cited pages differ: E-claude-code-00839 says subagents "can also spawn subagents of their own"; E-claude-code-07387 says a subagent lacks "by default the Agent tool itself to prevent recursion". | ev: E-claude-code-00839, E-claude-code-00935, E-claude-code-07387
- codex-cli [partial, verified] thread/list can filter to spawned descendants of a thread at any depth through ancestorThreadId. agents.enabled defaults to true and false disables multi-agent tools. Nested deep scan workers keep non-interactive approval settings. | limit: This filter is experimental and requires `capabilities.experimentalApi = true`. No cited quote states a depth limit or whether a subagent may itself spawn subagents. | ev: E-codex-cli-00283, E-codex-cli-00036, E-codex-cli-04718
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] The CLI enforces depth and concurrency limits to prevent runaway agent spawning. COPILOT_SUBAGENT_MAX_DEPTH sets maximum nesting depth (default 4, range 1-128); a settings.json depth setting (default 6, capped at 256) is honored only for usage-based billing users. code-review and security-review do not delegate a whole review to a nested review subagent. | limit: Docs disagree on the default depth: COPILOT_SUBAGENT_MAX_DEPTH default 4, range 1-128 (E-copilot-cli-01016) vs settings depth default 6, capped at 256, honored only for usage-based billing users (E-copilot-cli-01275). | ev: E-copilot-cli-01016, E-copilot-cli-01275, E-copilot-cli-01081, E-copilot-cli-01052
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents (default false) lets subagents invoke other subagents, up to a maximum nesting depth of five. A custom agent's agents field lists permitted subagents (* for all, [] to prevent any subagent use). chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits sets process-wide limits on recursive session creation. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00558, E-copilot-vscode-00122, E-copilot-vscode-01010, E-copilot-vscode-02648
- cursor [partial, verified] Since Cursor 2.5, subagents can launch child subagents within a nesting limit, forming a tree of coordinated work. The main agent and its direct subagents can launch subagents. The Python SDK docs state the same rule. | limit: A subagent launched by another subagent can't launch further ones (E-cursor-01432). Side chats: 'Nesting is not supported. A side chat cannot spawn its own side chats.' (E-cursor-04224) | ev: E-cursor-01432, E-cursor-01182, E-cursor-04224
- gemini-cli [supported, verified] Subagents cannot call other subagents. Even if a subagent is granted the `*` tool wildcard, it will still be unable to see or invoke other agents. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00426, E-gemini-cli-00499

## F09.built-in-agents — Built-in agent types

Definition: Agents shipped with the product and their defaults.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Built-in subagents include Explore, Plan, and general-purpose. Without a subagent_type, the Agent tool uses the built-in general-purpose subagent, even when you define no agents. The built-in Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md. Setting CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1 disables built-in subagent types and only applies in non-interactive mode (-p). | ev: E-claude-code-09483, E-claude-code-00841, E-claude-code-07623, E-claude-code-07972
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Codex ships with built-in agents, including worker (execution-focused agent for implementation and fixes) and explorer (read-heavy codebase exploration agent). If a custom agent name matches a built-in agent such as explorer, your custom agent takes precedence. | ev: E-codex-cli-00027, E-codex-cli-00028, E-codex-cli-00029, E-codex-cli-00043
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Copilot CLI includes built-in agents the main agent can run as subagents. The code-review agent is listed with model claude-sonnet-4.6; it analyzes diffs for bugs, security issues, and logic errors and will not modify code. The rubber duck agent is a built-in critic that gives a second opinion using a different AI model from the session. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00059, E-copilot-cli-01045, E-copilot-cli-00023
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] A built-in Plan agent researches the codebase, clarifies requirements, and proposes an implementation plan before code changes begin. Rubber Duck is a built-in, read-only critic that gives Copilot a second opinion on its plans, code, and tests. A built-in research agent produces thorough, well-cited reports. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00305, E-copilot-vscode-00725, E-copilot-vscode-00428
- cursor [supported, unverified] Cursor includes three built-in subagents (Explore, Bash, Browser) that handle context-heavy operations. Built-in subagents select their model automatically based on the subtask; the Explore subagent runs in its own context window with a faster model. Custom subagent names cannot collide with built-ins (explore, debug, shell, computerUse, etc.). | ev: E-cursor-01401, E-cursor-01457, E-cursor-00116, E-cursor-00391
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Codebase Investigator is a built-in subagent whose purpose is to analyze the codebase, reverse engineer, and understand complex (quote truncated). cli_help is enabled by default in Plan (Mode, per the heading). /agents list shows all discovered agents, including built-in, local (quote truncated). The Codebase Investigator section shows overrides in settings.json under agents.overrides. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00395, E-gemini-cli-00228, E-gemini-cli-00532, E-gemini-cli-00396
- grok-build [supported, unverified] Built-in types include `explore` (read, list, and search only; no shell, no edits) and `plan` (drafts an implementation plan; no shell, no edits). `GROK_AGENT` takes a built-in agent name, a profile, or an absolute path to an agent definition. `[subagents.toggle]` enables or disables individual subagent types. | ev: E-grok-build-00313, E-grok-build-00314, E-grok-build-00154, E-grok-build-00209
